newsitem.title: TURKEY: Five dead in Kurdish suicide bombing in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Five dead in Kurdish suicide bombing in Turkey.

text.p: A female Kurdish guerrilla killed herself and four other people on Tuesday in the second rebel suicide bombing in Turkey in five days, police said.
"We have three police martyrs," a police spokesman told Reuters. "The female terrorist and a civilian also died," he said.
He said the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel exploded a device inside a police car in the central town of Sivas after she had been picked up by police to be searched.
Security at public places throughout the country had been stepped up to ward off any PKK attacks on Tuesday's Republic Day national day celebrations.
A PKK suicide bomber killed herself and four other people in an attack on a police station in the southern city of Adana last Friday.
The rebels, fighting a 12-year-old campaign for Kurdish self rule in southeast Turkey, staged their first suicide bombing in July. Ten people died in that attack in the town of Tunceli.
PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan has threatened to stage a wave of suicide bombings.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the conflict.
